## 假期固定收益市場簡報

美國固定收益市場週五因獨立紀念日補假休市，沒有正常交易時段、完整紐約收盤，也沒有7月3日的美國債券價格發現。週四提早收盤後發布的消息，要到週一恢復正常交易才會首次反映；屆時投資人將面對聯準會近期升息預期進一步降溫、央行再受政治壓力，以及一週密集的美國公債供給。

假期期間最重要的政策變化，是美國與伊朗達成和平協議、帶動油價下跌後，市場全面重新評估還需要多少緊縮。美國就業成長轉弱、能源價格回落，使短期訊號不再那麼偏鷹；市場完全定價的首次升息25個基點時點延後至12月，下次會議升息機率則由本週稍早約三分之一降至20%以下。隨著投資人降低近期升息預期，黃金全週上漲2.2%，逼近每盎司$4,200。

這波重新定價仍未釐清政策前景。雖然6月非農就業僅增加57,000人，前2個月數據也遭下修，安聯與法國巴黎銀行的經濟學家仍認為美國通膨壓力足以要求今年再升息一次。安聯的Ludovic Subran預期通膨高點將超過3.7%，並認為9月仍可能升息；法國巴黎銀行的Isabelle Mateos y Lago則表示，就業報告疲弱降低7月升息的可能性，卻未削弱更廣泛的緊縮理由。相較之下，彭博經濟研究預期聯準會將在2026年全年維持利率不變，主席Kevin Warsh推動的制度檢討也提供另一項觀望理由。

最高法院阻止解除理事Lisa Cook職務後，總統Donald Trump及其盟友再度試圖重塑聯準會，使這場政策辯論增添治理風險。政府官員與外部顧問正研究以其他方式撤換理事、為Trump提名的人選製造空缺，Cook與前主席Jerome Powell仍是目標。判決強化了聯準會免受行政部門直接撤職的保障，但總統盟友認為，裁決聚焦程序問題，可能也為再次提出挑戰指明路徑。

歐洲政策討論的方向，與聯準會仍面臨的升息風險相反。歐洲央行官員為6月升息25個基點辯護，但愈來愈傾向將其形容為因應能源衝擊的保險措施，而這項衝擊其後已經消退。法國央行總裁Emmanuel Moulin表示，油價下跌且尚未出現明顯的二輪效應，使歐洲央行處於有利位置；他並重申，6月行動並非新一輪升息週期的起點。德國央行總裁Joachim Nagel的態度較為保留，警告中東和解與油價跌勢都可能逆轉，決策官員應保留所有選項。

亞洲則面臨另一組債券市場限制。中國人民銀行6月淨買入政府債券的金額，由5月的人民幣500億元降至100億元，為2025年10月恢復購債以來最低。這顯示北京希望維持充裕流動性，但不願鼓勵主權債殖利率再次大幅下跌；新設的隔夜公開市場操作，也提供更精準管理短期資金的替代工具。

日本方面，日圓徘徊在1986年以來最弱水準附近，財務省重申可能在不事先警告的情況下干預匯市。財務大臣片山皋月表示，日本與美國保持密切聯繫，必要時已準備採取行動，但她再次避免使用過去往往預示干預將至的更強硬措辭。日本央行最新估計顯示，第1季經濟產能仍略微偏緊，增添最終推動政策正常化的理由；不過油價下跌也降低了加快行動的必要性。

## 全球利率、信用與主權債情勢

歐洲央行6月升息仍是判斷歐洲公債的核心基準，但再次行動的理由已經轉弱。總裁Christine Lagarde表示，伊朗衝突造成的供給衝擊開始向整體經濟擴散後，管理委員會採取緊縮是正確決定。她將這些間接影響與二輪壓力區分開來，並表示後者尚未出現。Moulin同樣指出，油價下跌應可緩和服務業通膨，官員也未承諾連續升息。

Nagel則維持較偏鷹的立場。他表示，依據會議當時可取得的預測，6月行動無可避免，並警告不能假定中東敵對情勢已確定結束。他主張逐次會議決策，意味7月與9月都仍可能採取行動；愛爾蘭央行總裁Gabriel Makhlouf則強調，歐洲央行決心讓通膨回到2%。

民間經濟學家的看法也有分歧。Subran將6月行動形容為保險性升息，並認為這可能已是最後一次。Mateos y Lago仍預期9月會再升息，但也承認官員未釋出鷹派訊號，使暫停行動的可能性上升。現在爭論的焦點，不再是現貨油價本身是否足以支持進一步緊縮，而是先前的能源衝擊會不會延後傳導至食品、服務與薪資要求。

法國數據則增添成長轉弱的訊號。5月製造業產出下降1.0%，4月增幅經修正後為0.6%；其中運輸設備下降2.8%，電氣、電子及電腦設備減少2.3%，是主要拖累。工業總產出繼4月上升0.3%後，5月小幅下降0.1%。採礦、能源及供水產出增加3.2%，提供部分抵銷；3月至5月整體工業產出仍較2025年同期高出2.4%。

法國財政前景構成的主權風險，與工廠數據疲弱是兩個不同問題。總統Emmanuel Macron任內最後一場預算攻防逐漸成形，政府希望將赤字降至接近GDP的5%，僅略低於2025年的5.1%。總理Sebastien Lecornu警告，如果國會未能通過財政法案、現行法規必須延用，赤字可能擴大至6.5%。

政治時程也提高了失敗的代價。延後召開的公共財政警示委員會預計將討論新的支出限制，之後政府會在9月提出財政法案。自2024年以來，預算爭議已導致2位總理下台；如果方案遲遲無法解決，2027年4月總統大選後的下一屆政府也會受到牽制。法國尚未確立一條可在2029年前履行承諾、把赤字降至歐盟3%上限以內的路徑。

財政部長Roland Lescure表示發債進展順利，Moulin也說法國公債標售未遭遇困難。然而，隨著投資人開始聚焦2027年預算，法國10年期公債相對德國公債的利差升至約80個基點，創近9個月最寬。Macron執政10年期間，法國借款將增加逾€1.25兆，使下一屆政府更缺乏餘裕，難以承受政治進程再次延誤或經濟成長不如預期。

歐盟整體的對外收支狀況較為有利。經季節調整後，第1季經常帳盈餘由前一季的€992億、相當於GDP的2.1%，擴大至€1,134億、相當於GDP的2.4%。服務帳盈餘由€439億增至€521億，初次所得也由€43億赤字轉為€253億盈餘。這些改善足以抵銷商品帳盈餘由€890億降至€667億的影響。

丹麥克朗跌破過去通常會促使央行干預的水準，為歐洲利率前景帶來另一項不確定性。丹麥國家銀行容許克朗突破每歐元7.47後，匯率觸及每歐元7.4758克朗的歷史低點，使市場難以再按該國歐元聯繫匯率制度下的慣常框架預判政策。央行拒絕說明其容忍程度是否已經改變。

丹麥國家銀行正式規定克朗可在每歐元7.46038克朗上下2.25%的區間內波動，但實務上一直維持遠窄於此的範圍，通常會在調整利率前先以150億至200億丹麥克朗的規模干預匯市。丹麥公共財政穩健，使其政策利率得以維持在比歐洲央行低40個基點的水準。Nordea的Jan Storup Nielsen表示，丹麥擁有龐大經常帳盈餘，財政基本面也比先前承受壓力時更強，因此央行現在可能不再那麼擔心克朗溫和貶值。

丹麥企業的海外投資也可能降低克朗需求，因為跨國企業保留海外盈餘，用以資助外國工廠及其他計畫。如果丹麥國家銀行確實提高了干預門檻，單獨升息的可能性便隨之下降。其影響不只限於匯率：丹麥擁有全球規模最大的擔保債券市場之一，政策決定因而與家庭借款成本及投資人報酬緊密相連。

英國投資人同樣把短端政策前景與長期財政風險分開看待。Jupiter、Neuberger Berman及Royal London等資產管理公司對Andy Burnham維持借款紀律的承諾更有信心，但在下一任財政大臣人選及首份預算更加明朗前，仍不願持有長天期英國公債。英國公債2年期與10年期殖利率曲線利差為66個基點，是3月中旬以來最陡，且仍比美國與德國的可比曲線更陡峭。

油價下跌削弱了市場對英國央行今年必須緊縮的信念。貨幣市場顯示，年底前升息25個基點的機率為80%；6月時市場則至少已完全反映一次升息。部分投資人因而認為較短天期債券更具價值，退休基金的結構性需求疲弱則持續壓抑長端。

日本最新產能估計強化了國內應繼續考慮政策正常化的理由。日本央行估計第1季產出缺口為正0.53%，略低於第4季的0.57%；資本投入缺口貢獻0.44%，勞動投入缺口貢獻0.10%。2025會計年度下半年的估計潛在成長率由0.66%升至0.69%，但日本央行提醒，這兩項衡量都容易受方法選擇與估計誤差影響。

這組數據本身並不構成立即行動的理由。能源價格下跌可減輕輸入性通膨壓力，首相高市早苗也傾向漸進推動正常化。不過，產能仍偏緊，加上日圓極度疲弱，使日本央行必須權衡兩股力量：整體通膨的急迫性下降，但匯率貶值與國內資源吃緊仍可能支撐基礎價格壓力。

片山皋月表示，日本殖利率近期上升是多項因素共同造成，包括Warsh的談話、美國勞動數據疲弱，以及日本公債標售表現不佳。她否認政府最新經濟藍圖意在加強對日本央行的影響，並稱其中要求協調的文字只是標準用語。經濟產業大臣赤澤亮正另表示，面對中東衝擊與日圓疲弱造成的成本上升，政府正為中小企業提供融資與信用支援。

中國減少主權債購買，也反映當局擔心金融環境放鬆的副作用。6月淨買入人民幣100億元，較5月減少80%，是9個月來最不活躍的一個月。東方金誠的王青表示，中國人民銀行似乎希望殖利率大致穩定；如果10年期殖利率跌破1.70%，可能再次暫停債券交易。殖利率先前因下跌過多，促使人行在2025年1月至9月暫停購債。

新設的隔夜流動性操作，意味不能直接把購債減少解讀為全面緊縮。當中國人民銀行希望管理短期資金、但不願增加對長天期債券的需求時，這項工具可以取代政府債券購買。整體政策組合因此指向更精準的流動性控制：一方面支撐融資環境，另一方面避免現金過剩與借款成本急遽下降。

土耳其公布了假期期間幅度最大的實際通膨數據。6月消費者物價上升0.99%，年增32.11%，使年初至今漲幅達17.76%。單月整體漲幅相對受控，卻掩蓋民生必需類別持續承壓：食品及非酒精飲料年增35.45%，運輸上漲31.15%，住宅、水、電、瓦斯及其他燃料則攀升45.14%。12個月平均通膨率為32.03%。

油價下跌給予土耳其央行一些空間，可縮小40%有效融資利率與37%政策利率之間的差距，但6月通膨組成仍未化解實質利率與政策可信度問題。改善主要來自眼前能源價格衝擊減弱，住宅與食品成本卻仍高到足以讓通膨預期持續脆弱。

巴西政府則為定向擴張信用辯護，回應相關措施可能削弱貨幣緊縮效果的批評。財政部長Dario Durigan表示，針對特定產業的方案，包括一項供非正式工作者使用的新信用與債務協商計畫，並未阻止央行在最近一次會議採取更大幅度的降息。政府研究估計，這些措施可創造近200萬個就業機會，為GDP增加1,109億雷亞爾，並帶來454億雷亞爾稅收。

Durigan主張，3月以來通膨預期上升，主要反映外部及天候衝擊，而非信用方案。這項區別仍很重要，因為巴西央行雖在6月把Selic利率降至14.25%，卻已警告10月大選前刺激需求可能讓通膨降溫更加困難。當通膨預期惡化時，僅將信用措施限定於特定對象，並不能回答額外放款會如何影響總體需求。

信用市場仍向潛在交易開放。ICICI Bank正考慮透過全球中期票據計畫發行至少$5億境外債券；若成行，將是這家印度銀行自2017年發行$5億債券後，首次透過該計畫發行指標美元債。該行正與全球銀行合作，可能在未來數週進入市場。

這項計畫接續印度央行為符合資格的海外借款提供優惠外匯交換機制，目的在吸引全球資本並支撐盧比。HDFC Bank上月籌得$7.5億，Axis Bank、印度國家銀行及Power Finance Corp.也已進入國際市場融資。盧比自5月底跌至接近兌美元97盧比的歷史低點以來，已升值近2%。

歐洲槓桿融資方面，CVC Capital Partners計畫發行€12億高收益債券，為收購義大利食品原料製造商Irca籌資。這批債券將償還Barclays、法國巴黎銀行、HSBC與UBS提供的過橋貸款；這些銀行另提供一筆循環信用額度。債券預計在夏季過後發行。儘管投資人對非投資等級債券需求仍具韌性，市場目前仍以再融資及重新定價為主，這項潛在發行則增添了一筆收購融資交易。

與此同時，新興市場投資人正分散套利部位的融資幣別。AllianceBernstein與Invesco表示，已降低對美元融資的依賴，並納入歐元、加幣與日圓；Morgan Stanley則建議，以更廣泛的融資貨幣籃子表達對新興市場的樂觀看法。這項轉變反映市場對Warsh領導下聯準會所帶來的美元不確定性，並不代表投資人放棄較高收益貨幣。

HSBC調查101家合計管理$4,320億資產的機構後發現，美元走強已取代地緣政治，成為新興市場的首要疑慮；固定收益偏好則明顯轉向強勢貨幣債券。自美國於2025年4月宣布關稅以來，以美元融資、投資巴西雷亞爾、哥倫比亞披索及土耳其里拉的部位已回報26%，但聯準會若再度升息，套利優勢將會縮小。分散融資端的幣別，可以降低美元失序上漲的曝險，且不必對美元方向作出單一預測。

## 下一個交易時段觀察重點

美國固定收益市場將於7月6日週一恢復正常交易，假期期間的政策與總體消息屆時才會首次反映在美國公債價格。6月ISM服務業指數與紐約聯準銀行全球供應鏈壓力指數將於美東時間10:00公布。服務業需求、就業與價格將檢驗非農就業成長放緩是否已延伸至美國經濟最大的產業，物流指標則可顯示荷姆茲海峽交通恢復後，供給壓力已緩解到何種程度。

美國財政部的供給週期將於週一美東時間11:30展開，標售$920億91天期國庫券及$790億182天期國庫券，兩者均於7月9日交割。週二接著標售$900億42天期國庫券、$520億364天期國庫券，以及$580億3年期公債。附息債時程隨後包括週三增額發行$390億、票息4.375%的10年期公債，以及週四增額發行$220億、票息5.000%的30年期公債，兩者皆於7月15日交割。這一系列標售會先檢驗現金工具與短端債券需求，再測試對財政和期限溢價疑慮最敏感的長天期券種。

6月16日至17日FOMC會議紀要將於週三美東時間14:00公布。投資人將觀察委員會轉向鷹派背後的意見分布、通膨風險與勞動市場韌性之間的權衡，以及Warsh決定減少前瞻指引是否已產生初步影響。這份紀要早於疲弱的6月非農就業報告，其重要性在於揭示官員當時認為哪些條件足以支持再次升息，而不是確認官員如何回應後續數據。

日本5月暫定勞動調查將於週二日本時間08:30公布，現金薪資與實質工資可檢驗協商後的薪資增幅是否正轉化為家庭所得。日本央行操作及貨幣基礎數據於08:50公布，消費活動指數則排定於14:00發布。本週稍晚的放款數據與日本央行地區經濟報告，將進一步說明正產出缺口背後的信用、薪資、物價及經濟活動是否具有廣度。

紐西蘭央行將於週三紐西蘭時間14:00公布7月利率決策。5月會議票數相同，總裁Anna Breman投下決定票、使利率維持不變後，官方現金利率仍為2.25%。油價下跌降低輸入性物價衝擊長期延續的威脅，但如何在國內需求疲弱與利率回歸中性水準之間取捨仍未解決，使這次表決成為亞太地區主要利率事件之一。

美國5月貿易數據與紐約聯準銀行6月消費者預期調查將於週二公布，週四則發布截至7月4日當週的初領失業救濟金人數。在就業轉弱延後市場預期的聯準會升息時點、經濟學家卻繼續警告美國價格壓力持續之際，家庭通膨預期尤其重要。市場恢復交易後，首要問題已不再是假期是否造成美國公債波動，而是服務業通膨、通膨預期與標售需求，能否證明近期升息押注降溫具有依據。

overall_summary.headline: 油價下跌與就業轉弱延後聯準會升息預期，通膨與治理風險仍未消退
overall_summary.session_narrative:
美國固定收益市場因獨立紀念日補假休市，沒有正常交易時段、完整紐約收盤，也沒有7月3日的美國債券價格發現。美國與伊朗達成和平協議後油價下跌，加上6月非農就業僅增加57,000人，使市場完全定價的首次升息25個基點時點延後至12月；下次會議升息機率則由本週稍早約三分之一降至20%以下。經濟學家對通膨是否仍要求今年再次升息看法不一，總統Donald Trump的盟友又再度試圖重塑聯準會，增添治理風險。

歐洲方面，官員愈來愈傾向把歐洲央行6月升息25個基點形容為因應能源衝擊的保險措施，而這項衝擊其後已經消退；不過Joachim Nagel仍保留進一步行動的可能性。法國財政爭議則構成另一項主權風險：10年期法國公債相對德國公債的利差升至約80個基點，政府也警告，如果財政法案未能通過，赤字可能擴大至6.5%。

中國6月買入政府債券的金額由人民幣500億元降至100億元，同時保留可管理短期流動性的隔夜工具。日本產出缺口為正0.53%，日圓又極度疲弱，使日本央行最終推動政策正常化的理由仍在；但油價下跌已降低立即行動的急迫性。
overall_summary.summary: 美國固定收益市場因獨立紀念日補假休市；就業成長轉弱與油價下跌，使市場完全定價的首次聯準會升息時點延後至12月，但經濟學家對通膨的疑慮及央行再受政治壓力，令政策前景在週一恢復交易前仍未明朗。

section_summaries.summary: 能源衝擊消退，削弱歐洲央行再次升息的理由；法國預算僵局、丹麥克朗走弱及陡峭的英國公債殖利率曲線，則各自保留不同的歐洲風險。中國減少主權債購買，但未撤回對短期流動性的支持；日本產出缺口為正，使政策正常化仍在考量之列。儘管油價下跌，土耳其的通膨組成依然棘手。ICICI Bank與CVC的潛在債券發行顯示信用市場仍然開放，新興市場投資人則開始分散融資幣別。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Holiday Fixed-Income Brief

U.S. fixed-income markets were closed on Friday for Independence Day (observed), leaving no regular session, completed New York close or July 3 U.S. bond-price discovery. News released after Thursday’s early close therefore awaits the first regular session on Monday, when investors will confront a further retreat in immediate Federal Reserve tightening expectations, renewed political pressure on the central bank and a heavy week of Treasury supply.

The most consequential policy change over the holiday window was a broad reassessment of how much tightening remains necessary after the U.S.-Iran peace accord drove oil lower. The near-term evidence became less hawkish: softer U.S. employment growth and easing energy prices pushed the first fully priced quarter-point Fed increase back to December, while the probability assigned to a move at the next meeting fell below 20% from about one-third earlier in the week. Gold rose 2.2% over the week toward $4,200 an ounce as investors reduced expectations of an imminent increase.

That repricing did not settle the policy outlook. Economists at Allianz and BNP Paribas argued that U.S. inflation pressure remains sufficient to require another increase this year despite June payroll growth of only 57,000 and downward revisions to the prior 2 months. Allianz’s Ludovic Subran expects inflation to peak above 3.7% and said a September increase remains possible; BNP Paribas’s Isabelle Mateos y Lago said the weak employment report made July less likely without diminishing the broader case for tightening. Bloomberg Economics instead expects the Fed to remain on hold through 2026 as Chair Kevin Warsh’s institutional reviews provide another reason to wait.

The debate acquired a governance risk as President Donald Trump and his allies renewed efforts to reshape the Fed after the Supreme Court blocked an attempt to dismiss Governor Lisa Cook. Officials and outside advisers are exploring other ways to remove governors and create vacancies for Trump’s nominees, with Cook and former Chair Jerome Powell still among their targets. The ruling reinforced the Fed’s protection from direct executive removal, but allies of the president viewed its procedural focus as a possible roadmap for another challenge.

Europe’s policy discussion moved in the opposite direction from the Fed’s residual tightening risk. European Central Bank officials defended June’s 25-basis-point increase but increasingly described it as insurance against an energy shock that has since receded. Bank of France Governor Emmanuel Moulin said lower oil and the absence of visible second-round effects left the ECB in a good position and reiterated that June did not begin a new tightening cycle. Bundesbank President Joachim Nagel remained more guarded, warning that the Middle East settlement and oil decline could reverse and that officials should preserve all options.

Asia supplied a separate set of duration constraints. The People’s Bank of China reduced its net government-bond purchases to 10 billion yuan in June from 50 billion yuan in May, the smallest amount since purchases resumed in October 2025. The reduction suggested that Beijing wants ample liquidity without encouraging another sharp decline in sovereign yields, while its new overnight open-market operation gives it a more precise alternative for managing short-term funding.

In Japan, the Finance Ministry reiterated that it could intervene in foreign exchange without warning as the yen hovered near its weakest level since 1986. Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama said Japan remained in close contact with the U.S. and was prepared to act when necessary, although she again avoided the stronger language that has often preceded intervention. A new Bank of Japan estimate showed that economic capacity remained modestly stretched in the first quarter, adding to the case for eventual normalization even as cheaper oil reduces the need to accelerate.

## Global Rates, Credit, And Sovereign Developments

The ECB’s June increase remains the central reference point for European duration, but the justification for another move has weakened. President Christine Lagarde said the Governing Council was right to tighten after the Iran conflict’s supply shock began spreading through the economy. She distinguished those indirect effects from second-round pressure, which she said had not materialized. Moulin similarly said falling oil should soften services inflation and that officials were not committing to a sequence of increases.

Nagel preserved the hawkish qualification. He said June’s action had been unavoidable under the forecasts available at the meeting and warned against assuming that the end of Middle East hostilities was secure. His meeting-by-meeting stance leaves July and September open, while Irish central-bank Governor Gabriel Makhlouf stressed the ECB’s determination to return inflation to 2%.

Private-sector economists were also divided. Subran characterized June as an insurance increase that may prove to have been the final move. Mateos y Lago still expects another increase in September, but acknowledged that the lack of hawkish signaling from officials had widened the possibility of a pause. The dispute now concerns whether the earlier energy shock reaches food, services and wage demands with a lag, rather than whether spot oil alone warrants more tightening.

French data added a softer growth signal. Manufacturing output fell 1.0% in May after a revised 0.6% April increase, led by declines of 2.8% in transport equipment and 2.3% in electrical, electronic and computer equipment. Total industrial output slipped 0.1% after rising 0.3% in April. A 3.2% increase in mining, energy and water supply provided an offset, and whole-industry output during March through May was still 2.4% above the same period of 2025.

France’s fiscal outlook poses a separate sovereign risk from its weak factory data. President Emmanuel Macron’s final budget confrontation is forming around a deficit that the government wants to bring close to 5% of GDP, only marginally below 5.1% in 2025. Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu warned that the shortfall could widen to 6.5% if lawmakers fail to pass a finance bill and existing legislation must be rolled over.

The political calendar raises the cost of failure. A delayed public-finance alert committee is expected to consider new spending curbs, followed by presentation of the finance bill in September. Budget disputes have already brought down 2 prime ministers since 2024, and an unresolved plan could constrain the next government after the April 2027 presidential election. France has not yet established a path to meet its commitment to reduce the deficit within the EU’s 3% ceiling by 2029.

Finance Minister Roland Lescure said issuance was proceeding well, and Moulin said French auctions had encountered no difficulty. Yet the 10-year French spread over German debt reached about 80 basis points, the widest in almost 9 months, as investors began to focus on the 2027 budget. France’s borrowings will have increased by more than €1.25 trillion over Macron’s decade in office, leaving the next administration with less room to absorb another political delay or growth disappointment.

The broader EU external position was more favorable. The seasonally adjusted current-account surplus widened to €113.4 billion, or 2.4% of GDP, in the first quarter from €99.2 billion and 2.1% in the preceding quarter. The services surplus increased to €52.1 billion from €43.9 billion, while primary income swung to a €25.3 billion surplus from a €4.3 billion deficit. Those improvements more than offset a reduction in the goods surplus to €66.7 billion from €89 billion.

Denmark introduced another European rates uncertainty as the krone weakened beyond the level that had historically prompted central-bank intervention. The currency reached a record low of 7.4758 per euro after Nationalbanken allowed it to pass 7.47, challenging the usual framework for anticipating policy under the country’s euro peg. The central bank declined to explain whether its tolerance had changed.

Nationalbanken formally maintains the krone inside a 2.25% band around 7.46038 per euro but in practice has defended a much narrower range, typically intervening by 15 billion to 20 billion kroner before changing interest rates. Denmark’s strong public finances have allowed its policy rate to remain 40 basis points below the ECB’s. Nordea’s Jan Storup Nielsen said the bank may now be less concerned about modest weakness because Denmark has a large current-account surplus and stronger fiscal fundamentals than during earlier bouts of pressure.

Overseas investment by Danish companies may also have reduced demand for kroner as multinationals retain foreign earnings to finance factories and other projects abroad. If Nationalbanken has raised its intervention threshold, the prospect of a standalone rate increase has receded. That matters beyond the currency because Denmark has one of the world’s largest covered-bond markets, closely linking policy decisions to household borrowing costs and investor returns.

In Britain, investors were also separating front-end policy prospects from long-term fiscal risk. Asset managers including Jupiter, Neuberger Berman and Royal London expressed greater confidence in Andy Burnham’s promises of borrowing discipline but remained reluctant to own long-dated gilts before the identity of the next chancellor and the first budget become clearer. The 2s10s gilt curve was 66 basis points, its steepest level since mid-March, and remained steeper than comparable U.S. and German curves.

Lower oil has reduced conviction that the Bank of England will need to tighten this year. Money markets assigned an 80% probability to a quarter-point increase by year-end, compared with at least one full move priced during June. Some investors consequently saw more value in shorter maturities, while weak structural demand from pension funds continued to weigh on the long end.

Japan’s latest capacity estimates strengthened the domestic case for keeping normalization under consideration. The BOJ put the first-quarter output gap at positive 0.53%, down slightly from 0.57% in the fourth quarter. The capital-input gap contributed 0.44%, and the labor-input gap added 0.10%. Estimated potential growth for the second half of fiscal 2025 increased to 0.69% from 0.66%, although the BOJ cautioned that both measures are sensitive to methodology and estimation error.

The combination is not an argument for an immediate move by itself. Lower energy prices reduce imported inflation pressure, while Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi favors gradual normalization. But positive capacity utilization and the yen’s extreme weakness leave the BOJ balancing less urgent headline inflation against the possibility that currency depreciation and tight domestic resources sustain underlying price pressure.

Katayama attributed the recent increase in Japanese yields to several factors, including Warsh’s comments, weak U.S. labor data and a soft JGB auction. She rejected the view that the government’s latest economic blueprint sought greater influence over the BOJ, saying its call for coordination used standard language. Trade Minister Ryosei Akazawa separately said the government was supporting financing and credit for smaller companies facing higher costs from the Middle East shock and the weak currency.

China’s reduction in sovereign purchases likewise reflected concern about the side effects of easier financial conditions. June’s 10 billion yuan net buying was down 80% from May and marked the least active month in 9 months. Golden Credit Rating’s Wang Qing said the PBOC appears to prefer broadly stable yields and could again suspend bond transactions if the 10-year rate falls below 1.70%. The purchases had previously been halted from January through September 2025 after yields declined too far.

The new overnight liquidity operation complicates a direct reading of the purchase reduction as broad tightening. It can substitute for government-bond buying when the PBOC wants to manage short-term cash without adding long-duration demand. The policy mix therefore points to more precise liquidity control: support for funding conditions alongside resistance to excessive cash and sharply lower borrowing costs.

Turkey delivered the holiday window’s largest realized inflation reading. Consumer prices rose 0.99% in June and 32.11% from a year earlier, taking the year-to-date increase to 17.76%. The relatively contained monthly headline masked persistent pressure in essential categories: food and non-alcoholic beverages rose 35.45% from a year earlier, transportation increased 31.15%, and housing, water, electricity, gas and other fuels climbed 45.14%. The 12-month average inflation rate was 32.03%.

Cheaper oil gives Turkey’s central bank some room to reduce the gap between its 40% effective funding rate and the 37% policy rate, but the composition of June inflation leaves real-rate and credibility questions unresolved. The improvement is strongest in the immediate energy impulse, while housing and food costs remain high enough to keep expectations vulnerable.

Brazil’s government defended its own targeted credit expansion against criticism that it could weaken monetary restraint. Finance Minister Dario Durigan said programs aimed at specific sectors, including a new credit and debt-renegotiation initiative for informal workers, did not prevent the central bank from cutting more aggressively at its latest meeting. Government studies estimated that the measures could create nearly 2 million jobs, add 110.9 billion reais to GDP and generate 45.4 billion reais in tax revenue.

Durigan argued that higher inflation expectations since March chiefly reflect external and weather shocks rather than the credit programs. The distinction remains important because Brazil’s central bank reduced the Selic rate to 14.25% in June but has warned that demand stimulus before the October election could complicate disinflation. Targeting alone does not resolve the question of how additional credit affects aggregate demand when inflation expectations are deteriorating.

Credit markets remained open for prospective transactions. ICICI Bank is considering at least $500 million of offshore bonds under its global medium-term note program, which would be its first benchmark U.S. dollar offering through the facility since a $500 million sale in 2017. The Indian lender is working with global banks and could approach the market in coming weeks.

The plan follows the Reserve Bank of India’s concessional foreign-exchange swap facility for eligible overseas borrowing, intended to attract global capital and support the rupee. HDFC Bank raised $750 million last month, while Axis Bank, State Bank of India and Power Finance Corp. have also tapped international markets. The rupee has strengthened nearly 2% since reaching a record low near 97 per dollar in late May.

In European leveraged finance, CVC Capital Partners plans €1.2 billion of high-yield bonds to fund its acquisition of Italian food-ingredients maker Irca. The notes would refinance a bridge supplied by Barclays, BNP Paribas, HSBC and UBS, alongside a revolving facility from the banks. The bond sale is expected after the summer. Its prospective launch adds acquisition financing to a market still dominated by refinancing and repricing, despite resilient demand for speculative-grade debt.

Emerging-market investors, meanwhile, are diversifying the currencies used to fund carry positions. AllianceBernstein and Invesco said they were relying less exclusively on dollars and incorporating euros, Canadian dollars and yen, while Morgan Stanley recommended expressing EM optimism against a broader funding basket. The shift reflects uncertainty about the dollar under the Warsh Fed rather than abandonment of higher-yielding currencies.

An HSBC survey of 101 institutions managing a combined $432 billion found a stronger dollar had replaced geopolitics as the leading EM concern, while fixed-income preferences shifted decisively toward hard-currency debt. Dollar-funded positions in the Brazilian real, Colombian peso and Turkish lira have returned 26% since the U.S. tariff announcements of April 2025, but another Fed increase would narrow the carry advantage. Diversifying the funding leg reduces exposure to a disorderly dollar rise without requiring a single directional forecast for the currency.

## Next Open-Session Watch

Regular U.S. fixed-income trading resumes Monday, July 6, providing the first session in which the holiday window’s policy and macro news can enter Treasury prices. June ISM services and the New York Fed’s Global Supply Chain Pressure Index arrive at 10:00 ET. Services demand, employment and prices will test whether the slowdown in payroll growth extends into the economy’s largest sector, while the logistics gauge will show how far recovering Strait of Hormuz traffic has reduced supply pressure.

Treasury’s supply cycle begins Monday with $92 billion of 91-day bills and $79 billion of 182-day bills at 11:30 ET, both settling July 9. Tuesday brings $90 billion of 42-day bills, $52 billion of 364-day bills and a $58 billion 3-year note. The coupon calendar then moves to a $39 billion reopening of the 4.375% 10-year note on Wednesday and a $22 billion reopening of the 5.000% 30-year bond on Thursday, both settling July 15. The sequence will test demand first for cash instruments and front-end duration, then for the longer maturities most exposed to fiscal and term-premium concerns.

The June 16–17 FOMC minutes are due Wednesday at 14:00 ET. Investors will look for the distribution of views behind the Committee’s hawkish shift, the balance between inflation risk and labor resilience, and any early effect from Warsh’s decision to reduce forward guidance. The minutes predate the weak June payroll result, so their importance lies in revealing the conditions officials believed would justify another increase rather than confirming the subsequent data response.

Japan’s May provisional labor survey arrives Tuesday at 08:30 JST, with cash earnings and real wages testing whether negotiated pay gains are reaching household income. BOJ operations and monetary-base data follow at 08:50 JST, and the consumption activity index is scheduled for 14:00. Later in the week, lending data and the BOJ’s regional economic report will add evidence on the breadth of credit, wages, prices and activity behind the positive output gap.

The Reserve Bank of New Zealand announces its July decision Wednesday at 14:00 NZST. Its official cash rate was 2.25% after May’s evenly split meeting, when Governor Anna Breman’s casting vote produced a hold. Lower oil has reduced the threat of a prolonged imported-price shock, but the unresolved division between weak domestic demand and the path back toward a neutral policy setting makes the vote a principal Asia-Pacific rates event.

U.S. May trade data and the New York Fed’s June Survey of Consumer Expectations arrive Tuesday, followed Thursday by initial claims for the week ended July 4. Household inflation expectations will be particularly important after weaker employment delayed the expected Fed move while economists continued to warn about persistent U.S. price pressure. The first open-session question is no longer whether the holiday produced a Treasury move; it is whether services inflation, expectations and auction demand validate the retreat in near-term tightening bets once price discovery resumes.

section_summaries.summary: The holiday closure deferred U.S. price discovery as weaker employment and cheaper oil reduced immediate Fed tightening expectations. The first fully priced increase moved to December, but persistent inflation concerns, competing forecasts for the policy path and renewed political pressure on Fed governors prevented a settled conclusion. Europe leaned toward less tightening, while China and Japan continued to balance liquidity or normalization against sovereign-yield and currency risks.

section_summaries.section_title: Global Rates, Credit, And Sovereign Developments
section_summaries.summary: The case for another ECB increase weakened as the energy shock receded, while France’s budget impasse, Denmark’s weaker krone and Britain’s steep gilt curve preserved distinct European risks. China reduced sovereign purchases without withdrawing short-term liquidity support, and Japan’s positive output gap kept normalization in view. Turkey’s inflation composition remained difficult despite cheaper oil. Credit markets stayed open through prospective ICICI Bank and CVC bond sales, while EM investors diversified their funding currencies.

Monday’s reopening brings June ISM services and supply-chain data before a week of bill and coupon auctions tests demand from cash instruments through the 30-year sector. Wednesday’s FOMC minutes will show the distribution behind the Committee’s hawkish shift before the weak payroll report. Japan’s wage and BOJ data, the RBNZ’s divided rate decision, U.S. trade and inflation-expectations data, and jobless claims provide further tests of wages, imported inflation and labor cooling.

methodology_note: SIFMA recommends a full U.S. fixed-income market close for U.S. Independence Day (observed). No prior-session market levels are presented as current-day moves.

overall_summary.headline: Lower oil and weaker employment delayed Fed tightening expectations, but inflation and governance risks persisted
overall_summary.session_narrative:
U.S. fixed-income markets were closed for Independence Day (observed), leaving no regular session, completed New York close or July 3 U.S. bond-price discovery. Lower oil after the U.S.-Iran peace accord and June payroll growth of 57,000 pushed the first fully priced quarter-point Fed increase to December, while the probability of a move at the next meeting fell below 20% from about one-third earlier in the week. Economists remained divided over whether inflation still requires another increase this year, and renewed efforts by President Donald Trump’s allies to reshape the Fed added governance risk.

In Europe, officials increasingly described the ECB’s June 25-basis-point increase as insurance against an energy shock that has since receded, although Joachim Nagel kept further action open. France’s fiscal dispute remained a separate sovereign concern as its 10-year spread over German debt reached about 80 basis points and the government warned that the deficit could widen to 6.5% without a finance bill.

China reduced June government-bond purchases to 10 billion yuan from 50 billion yuan while retaining an overnight tool for short-term liquidity management. Japan’s positive 0.53% output gap and the yen’s extreme weakness sustained the case for eventual BOJ normalization, even as cheaper oil reduced the urgency to move.
overall_summary.summary: With U.S. fixed-income markets closed for Independence Day (observed), softer payroll growth and lower oil pushed the first fully priced Fed increase to December, while economists’ inflation concerns and renewed political pressure on the central bank left the policy outlook unresolved ahead of Monday’s reopening.
